## Observed Facts

Data Scope: Dataset OpenStack, all time ranges, level = WARNING, grouped by component.

Four Components emit WARNING Log Entries, 3,118 in total [E1]:

| Component | WARNING Log Entries | Share of 3,118 |
|---|---|---|
| nova.virt.libvirt.imagecache | 3,059 [E1] | ~98.1% |
| nova.compute.manager | 45 [E1] | ~1.4% |
| nova.virt.libvirt.driver | 12 [E1] | ~0.4% |
| keystonemiddleware.auth_token | 2 [E1] | ~0.1% |

The shares are my arithmetic on the counts in [E1].

## Hypotheses

- Nearly all WARNING volume comes from `nova.virt.libvirt.imagecache`. A single recurring warning type from one Component is the likely driver, so fixing or silencing it would remove most of the WARNING noise. This is a guess from the counts alone; I have not read the messages.
- The other three Components produce low volume. Their warnings are unlikely to be a priority unless the Team Lead has a separate reason to watch them.

## Unknowns

- The logs do not show what the imagecache warnings say or whether they point to a real fault. I did not retrieve sample messages in this step.
- I did not check whether these counts are steady, growing, or from a one-off spike. A trend query would show that.
- The counts do not show how many distinct incidents they represent. Log Entries are not incidents.

## Next Step

Pull sample messages for `nova.virt.libvirt.imagecache` WARNING entries, then run a daily trend on that Component to see whether the volume is steady or bursty. Start there because it accounts for about 98% of WARNING Log Entries [E1].
